name: Microsoft
summary: Microsoft reported higher cloud revenue in FY2025. The research question is how much of that demand translates into cash after the cost of adding capacity.
thesis: The cloud franchise is strengthening, but cash generation after infrastructure investment matters more than revenue growth alone.
counterargument: New capacity can cost cash before it is fully utilized. Strong sales may coexist with weaker cash conversion if investment stays elevated.
watch: Operating cash flow versus cash additions to property and equipment
Cloud revenue growth and gross margin
Whether added capacity is matched by sustained customer demand

claims.title: Cloud revenue rose year over year in the third quarter
claims.detail: Microsoft Cloud revenue was $42.4 billion in FY2025 Q3, versus $35.2 billion a year earlier.
claims.section: 10-Q · Part I, Item 2 · Management’s Discussion and Analysis

claims.title: Operating profit rose faster than sales in FY2025
claims.detail: Revenue increased about 15% year over year and operating income about 17%.
claims.section: 10-K · Part II, Item 7 · Results of Operations

claims.title: Cash from operations reached $136.2 billion
claims.detail: Cash from operations increased from $118.5 billion. The cash flow statement reports investment in property and equipment separately.
claims.section: 10-K · Part II, Item 8 · Cash Flows Statements

timeline.title: Associated Press coverage of the third-quarter release

revisions.title: Quarterly snapshot
revisions.detail: The quarter supported a cloud demand thesis. Annual cash conversion was still an open question.

revisions.title: Annual review
revisions.detail: The annual filing confirmed higher operating cash flow. The thesis puts more weight on what remains after infrastructure spending.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.detail: New capacity fills quickly. Cloud growth and cash generation improve together.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.detail: Demand grows while ongoing capacity spending limits near-term cash conversion.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.detail: Customers expand more slowly than expected, leaving Microsoft with the cost of capacity ahead of demand.

event.title: FY2025 Q3 earnings
event.context: Microsoft released earnings after the April 30 regular session. May 1 is the first regular session after the release. Other events can affect both series.
